content:
While AirPods with cameras are not expected to launch until next year, a Bloomberg report suggests Apple may unveil AirPods 5 at next month's iPhone event. Here are the details.

AirPods 5 will come in two versions: a standard model and an Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) model.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman stated in an extensive report published earlier tonight that Apple may announce a new Mac mini within the next few days, earlier than the expected September event.

Gurman also revealed several other new products in Apple's lineup, including AirPods 5, which may make its debut next month. He said the company's next event is expected to be held on September 9, which will also see the launch of its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro series, and new Apple Watch models.

The report reads as follows:

Apple is also preparing a series of minor updates for its Apple Watch lineup, including upgraded fitness tracking features and a new ceramic case option for the Series 12 model. The company also plans to debut new AirPods at its September product event. According to people familiar with the matter, the new lineup will include AirPods 5, an update to Apple's entry-level earbuds. The last model update was in 2024. As for the version of AirPods equipped with cameras, it is not expected to arrive until next year.

Interestingly, Gurman later added on social media platform X that AirPods 5 is expected to come in two versions: standard and noise-cancelling:

While reports about the AirPods 5 launch timeline have been scarce, the industry generally expects these earbuds to arrive until 2027. Apple is also reportedly developing two versions of AirPods with cameras, which will provide AI features through Visual Intelligence and Siri.

Apple previously accidentally included a demo video of AirPods with cameras in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, though the clip did not clearly show any differences in the device's appearance.
